thesis: Sequence transduction does not require recurrence or convolution: the Transformer, built on attention alone, reaches higher BLEU on two machine translation tasks while being far more parallelisable and markedly cheaper to train.
plainSummary: Until 2017 the standard for machine translation was the recurrent network, which processes words one after another. That sequential dependency is what made training hard to parallelise. This paper removes recurrence and convolution entirely and puts attention in their place. Inside every layer each position can look directly at every other; order is supplied separately, by sinusoidal position encodings added to the input embeddings. The result: 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German, more than 2 BLEU above the previous best including ensembles, at a small fraction of their training cost. The paper also shows the architecture generalises to English constituency parsing without task-specific tuning. The trade-off is stated plainly: the cost of self-attention grows with the square of the sequence length.
researchQuestion: If recurrent and convolutional layers are removed from a sequence transduction model and replaced entirely by attention, what happens to translation quality, parallelisability and training cost?
methods: Encoder and decoder were each built as a stack of six identical layers, with every sub-layer wrapped in a residual connection followed by layer normalisation.
The attention function is Scaled Dot-Product Attention: query-key dot products are divided by √d_k before the softmax.
Instead of a single attention, h = 8 parallel heads are used, each operating at d_k = d_v = 64.
Masking in the decoder ensures position i can depend only on known outputs at positions before i, preserving the auto-regressive property.
Order information is injected through sine and cosine functions of different frequencies, added to the learned embeddings.
Each layer contains a position-wise feed-forward network with a ReLU in between two linear transformations (d_model = 512, d_ff = 2048).
Training ran on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs, using Adam with a custom learning rate schedule that warms up over 4000 steps.
Regularisation combined residual dropout (P_drop = 0.1) with label smoothing of 0.1.
Models were trained on WMT 2014 English-German (about 4.5M sentence pairs) and English-French (36M sentences); beam search was used at inference.
The contribution of each component was measured through ablations on the newstest2013 development set, varying head count, d_k, model size, dropout and position encoding.
Generalisation was probed by training a 4-layer Transformer for English constituency parsing on the Penn Treebank WSJ portion.
findings: Transformer (big) reached 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German, beating the previous best results — including ensembles — by more than 2 BLEU.
Table 2 lists 41.8 BLEU for the big model on English-to-French, obtained after 3.5 days of training on eight GPUs.
Even the base model surpassed every previously published model and ensemble, at an estimated 3.3 · 10^18 FLOPs — a fraction of its competitors' cost.
A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, O(1), where a recurrent layer requires O(n).
Single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, but quality also drops when too many heads are used.
Learned positional embeddings produce nearly identical results to the sinusoidal encoding; the sinusoidal version was chosen in the hope it would extrapolate to longer sequences.

A 4-layer Transformer reached 92.7 F1 on WSJ Section 23 in the semi-supervised setting without task-specific tuning, beating every previously reported model except the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar.
limitations: Self-attention costs O(n² · d) per layer; the paper concedes it is faster than a recurrent layer only while the sequence length n stays below the representation dimension d.
The restricted self-attention proposed for long sequences was never measured — it is explicitly left to future work.
The English-to-French result is reported inconsistently: the body of Section 6.1 says 41.0 BLEU while the abstract and Table 2 say 41.8.
Averaging attention-weighted positions reduces effective resolution; the paper claims multi-head attention counteracts this but never quantifies the compensation.
The interpretability claim is qualitative — phrased with 'could' and 'appear to' — and no numerical measure of interpretability is offered.
Evaluation covers two translation directions and a single parsing task, and the paper notes only a small number of hyperparameter experiments were run for parsing.
The training-cost FLOP figures were not measured but estimated by multiplying training time, GPU count and an assumed sustained throughput per GPU.

claimStatements.claim-background-01: The inherently sequential nature of recurrent models precludes parallelisation within a training example, and the constraint becomes critical at longer sequence lengths.
claimStatements.claim-background-02: In convolution-based alternatives the number of operations needed to relate two distant positions grows with distance: linearly for ConvS2S, logarithmically for ByteNet.
claimStatements.claim-method-01: The Transformer is a network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
claimStatements.claim-method-02: The encoder is a stack of six identical layers; each combines multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network, both wrapped in a residual connection and layer normalisation.
claimStatements.claim-method-03: The decoder inserts a third sub-layer that performs multi-head attention over the output of the encoder stack.
claimStatements.claim-method-04: Masking in the decoder, combined with offsetting the output embeddings by one position, guarantees that the prediction for position i depends only on known outputs at positions less than i.
claimStatements.claim-method-05: The attention function is Scaled Dot-Product Attention: query-key dot products are divided by √d_k, passed through a softmax, and used to take a weighted sum of the values.
claimStatements.claim-method-06: The model uses 8 parallel attention heads with d_k = d_v = d_model / h = 64, so the total computational cost stays comparable to single-head attention at full dimensionality.
claimStatements.claim-method-07: The position-wise feed-forward network has input and output dimension d_model = 512 and an inner dimension d_ff = 2048.
claimStatements.claim-method-08: Because the model contains no recurrence and no convolution, order is injected via sine and cosine functions of different frequencies, added to embeddings of the same dimension.
claimStatements.claim-method-09: Training ran on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs; the base model for 100,000 steps (12 hours) and the big model for 300,000 steps (3.5 days).
claimStatements.claim-method-10: The learning rate followed a schedule that increases linearly for the first 4000 warmup steps and then decays proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number.
claimStatements.claim-method-11: Regularisation used dropout at P_drop = 0.1 on sub-layer outputs plus label smoothing of 0.1; the label smoothing hurt perplexity while improving accuracy and BLEU.
claimStatements.claim-method-12: Training data was the standard WMT 2014 English-German set of about 4.5 million sentence pairs, encoded with a shared byte-pair vocabulary of roughly 37000 tokens.
claimStatements.claim-result-01: Transformer (big) established a new state of the art of 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German, beating the best previously reported models — ensembles included — by more than 2.0 BLEU.
claimStatements.claim-result-02: Table 2 lists 41.8 BLEU for the big model on English-to-French, and the abstract states the result was reached after 3.5 days of training on eight GPUs.
claimStatements.claim-result-03: The base model produced 27.3 BLEU (EN-DE) and 38.1 (EN-FR) at an estimated 3.3 · 10^18 FLOPs, surpassing every previously published model and ensemble at a fraction of the cost.
claimStatements.claim-result-04: A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations while a recurrent layer requires O(n); Table 1 gives self-attention a per-layer cost of O(n² · d) and a maximum path length of O(1).
claimStatements.claim-result-05: In the ablations, single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, but quality also degrades when the head count is pushed too high.
claimStatements.claim-result-06: Replacing the sinusoidal position encoding with learned positional embeddings produces nearly identical results to the base model.
claimStatements.claim-result-07: A 4-layer Transformer reached 91.3 F1 on WSJ Section 23 training on WSJ alone and 92.7 F1 in the semi-supervised setting, beating all previously reported models except the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar.
claimStatements.claim-interpretation-01: The authors state they suspect that for large d_k the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing softmax into regions of extremely small gradients; the √d_k scaling is a precaution based on that supposition.
claimStatements.claim-interpretation-02: The authors say they chose the sinusoidal version because it may let the model extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than those seen in training — a hypothesis, not a measured result.
claimStatements.claim-interpretation-03: Interpretability is presented as a side benefit rather than a measured result: attention heads are said to 'appear' to exhibit behaviour related to syntactic and semantic structure.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-01: Self-attention is faster than a recurrent layer only while the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimension d; because its cost grows quadratically in n, that advantage disappears on long sequences.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-02: The restricted self-attention proposed to reduce cost on very long sequences was not tried in this paper; it is explicitly deferred to future work.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-03: The English-to-French result is reported inconsistently: Section 6.1 states 41.0 BLEU while the abstract and Table 2 give 41.8 BLEU for the same model.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-04: Averaging attention-weighted positions reduces effective resolution; the paper states multi-head attention counteracts this but never quantifies by how much.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-05: The paper states that only a small number of hyperparameter experiments were run for the parsing task, so those results are not the product of a systematic search.
claimStatements.claim-limitation-06: The training-cost FLOP figures in Table 2 are estimates, not measurements: they were derived by multiplying training time, GPU count and an assumed sustained single-precision throughput per GPU.
claimStatements.claim-repro-01: The authors state that the code used to train and evaluate the models is available in the tensor2tensor repository.

metric-bleu-ende-big: WMT 2014 English-German newstest2014; more than 2.0 BLEU above the previous best
metric-bleu-enfr-big: WMT 2014 English-French newstest2014; the body of Section 6.1 says 41.0 for the same model
metric-flops-big: Estimated as time × GPU count × assumed sustained throughput
metric-flops-base: A fraction of what competing models cost
metric-train-days-big: 300,000 steps on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs
metric-train-hours-base: 100,000 steps on 8 P100 GPUs, about 0.4 seconds per step
metric-dmodel: Output dimension of every sub-layer and of the embedding layers
metric-heads: Parallel attention layers in the base model
metric-dff: Hidden layer of the position-wise feed-forward network
metric-warmup: The phase over which the learning rate rises linearly
metric-params-big: The big configuration in the last row of Table 3
metric-ppl-big: newstest2013; per word-piece, not comparable to per-word figures

glossary.definition: The problem of mapping one sequence of symbols to another; machine translation is the canonical case.
A function mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output computed as a weighted sum of the values, where each weight comes from the compatibility of the query with the corresponding key.
An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of that sequence; also called intra-attention.
Projecting queries, keys and values h times through different learned linear projections into a lower dimension, running attention in parallel, then concatenating and projecting the results.
Sine and cosine vectors of the same dimension as the embeddings, added to them so that a model without recurrence still receives order information.
The longest distance a forward or backward signal must travel between any two input or output positions; shorter paths make long-range dependencies easier to learn.
A regulariser that leaves some uncertainty in the target distribution instead of concentrating it on a single point; here it hurt perplexity while improving BLEU.
Generating each symbol while consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input.
